I'm working through a graph construction problem: I need 20 vertices that are 3-colorable with girth at least 7 and at least 21 edges. Starting with a 20-cycle gives me 20 edges with infinite girth and 2-colorability, so I just need to add one more edge as a chord that creates cycles of length at least 7.

If I add a chord from vertex 0 to vertex 7, it creates two cycles: one of length 8 (going 0→1→2→...→7→0) and one of length 14 (going 0→7→8→...→19→0). Since both lengths are at least 7, the girth is 8. The chord connects vertices of different parity in the bipartite cycle, so the graph stays bipartite and therefore 3-colorable. This gives me exactly 21 edges with all requirements satisfied.
